source_ref: PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0221754 S1 File (journal.pone.0221754.s001, SPSS .sav) -- SPSS variable labels for Activist_1..Activist_8 and their value label sets labels17-labels24; paper Measures section ('Activism') for the scale name and the 0-to-5 response format.
note: Item codes ARE the source .sav column names: data/dwyer_2019_clinton_activism.py melts ACTIVIST_COLS = [f'Activist_{i}' for i in 1..8] with var_name='item', so no rename or positional assignment occurs and the .sav's own variable labels tie each code to its text. Wording is those variable labels verbatim (e.g. Activist_1 = 'Being an activist is central to who I am.'); the paper quotes two of them as sample items, 'Being an activist is central to who I am.' (Activist_1) and "I make time for activism, even when I'm busy." (Activist_4), matching the labels character for character. option_text comes from the value labels, with the leading '0 = ' .. '5 = ' numbering stripped (see public_note) and no other change. No instructions text is published anywhere in the deposit or the paper, so that field is blank rather than filled from a canonical AICS rendering. Rights: instrument is Klar & Kasser's (2009) Activist Identity and Commitment Scale; no fee, no-redistribution, non-commercial or permission-required clause could be located for it, and IRW's wording came from the CC BY 4.0 PLOS deposit's own SPSS labels, so silence-is-permission applies and no register row was written.
public_note: Respondents answered the Activist Identity and Commitment Scale on a 0-to-5 scale, but IRW stores the SPSS codes 1-6, so each resp value is one higher than the number on the scale the respondent saw; option_text gives the anchor wording for the corresponding point.

source_ref: Kumlander, Lahtinen, Turunen & Salmivalli (2018), PLOS ONE 13(12):e0207706, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0207706 -- S1 Table (Finnish + English items and W1/W2 Likert anchors) and S2 Table (W1 standardized loadings), figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.7426262 (CC BY 4.0); SPSS variable labels in pone.0207706.s006.sav; rights from https://self-compassion.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/SCS-information.pdf
note: Code derivation: data/kumlander_2018_self_compassion.py renames scompN_1 -> scompN by regex (^(scomp\d+)_1$), a number-preserving rename of the source column name -- core model section 3 pattern 2, nothing positional. The .sav's own variable labels read 'Self compassion scale N' and mark exactly {1,8,11,16,21,4,13,18,25,2,6,20,24} as '(neg)', which is Neff's reverse-scored set exactly; S1 Table numbers the items 1-26 and S2/S3 Tables key their loadings to SCOMP1..SCOMP26. mapping_basis=paper_explicit rather than data_labels because the variable labels give the item NUMBER, not the item's words -- the words are indexed to the code through S1 Table's numbering, which is an explicit code-to-item tie in the study's own supplement but not a label carrying the text. Verified against the data anyway: see verification_kumlander_2018_scs.csv / verify_kumlander_2018_scs.R. text_source=study_materials: both the Finnish and the English come from S1 Table of this study's supplement, not from Neff's own sheet (the two English renderings differ slightly, e.g. item 7 reads 'When I'm down and out' in S1 Table and 'When I'm down' on Neff's 2021 sheet; S1 Table's is what ships). translation_source=mixed: item_text_translated is the study's own English throughout; option_text_translated is the study's English for resp 1 and 5 and IRW's rendering for resp 2-4, which the study left in Finnish only (see notes_kumlander_2018_scs.csv). instructions left blank -- no Finnish instruction text is published. Rights: Neff's SCS information sheet grants permission 'for any purpose whatsoever' with no reserved right; quote, URL and sha256 in notes_kumlander_2018_scs.csv.
public_note: English for the three middle response anchors (resp 2, 3 and 4) was rendered by IRW from the Finnish; the study published English only for the two endpoints, and the Finnish in option_text is what respondents actually read.
